claims.assertion: The trip was metered RydeTAXI, so extra kilometres driven enter the fare directly: actual 31.0 km versus an optimal 20.6 km (+10.4 km, +50%), billed as $14.64 excess distance (10.38 km × $1.4100/km).
The GPS track contains two off-route segments: 18:46–18:56 added 5.66 km and 19:03–19:12 added 4.78 km, each therefore a separate segment requiring its own RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 justification.

The rider's consent at 18:43 — 'Sure, your call.' (Chat #2) — was given before the first segment started at 18:46 in answer to the driver's proposal to 'go round via Rifle Range Road', so it is a general route authorisation for reaching the destination, and it cannot reach the second, unannounced detour at 19:03–19:12.

Even for the first segment, the agreed named road is not tied to the driving by any record: no fact shows the vehicle on Rifle Range Road, and the segment roams up to 1923 m from the optimal route, so at most this segment is undetermined (G13) and it carries no refund; the second segment was never discussed at all — the driver's own statement admits 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting' and no message of the rider's approves it.

No traffic justification exists for the second detour: both expressways in the corridor (BKE and PIE) were only at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h), not band 1–2, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window, so RD-4 (a) and (b) both fail.

The second, unexempted segment therefore refunds 4.78 km × $1.4100/km = $6.74 (rounded to the cent), using the trip's per-km rate derived from the fare facts, and no other kilometre difference is claimed.

The driver's 90-day record shows 3 disputes with 1 upheld (no route cases upheld), which does not by itself make this case 'repeated' under RD-6, so no account flag is requested on the established count.

weaknesses: The rider did give a broad, timestamped consent covering the first deviation ('Sure, your call.' — F10 in reply to F9), so the first, larger 5.66 km segment (F3) is likely shielded by RD-5 and the driver will argue it covers both legs of the rerouting.

The 30–39 km/h band 4 reading on BKE (F13) and PIE (F14) gives the driver a rhetorical 'there was congestion' argument under the rider's own complaint about a jam, even though RD-4 requires band 1–2 or an incident (F15) for an exemption.
Some of the +10.4 km excess (F1) is not attributed to any gps-detour segment, and RD-2 expressly leaves unattributed mileage differences unrefunded, which caps the recovery at the segment figure.
